description: Felipe destaca-se pelo seu protagonismo e pela busca contínua por evolução. Apaixonado por mecânica e agronomia, une o conhecimento prático ao amor pela terra e pelas máquinas, demonstrando dedicação e curiosidade em tudo o que faz. Com seu jeito acolhedor e atencioso, fortalece o trabalho em equipe e inspira todos ao seu redor. Sua determinação em aprender e crescer a cada dia o torna uma liderança natural e um exemplo de empenho.

details:
CLIMATEAGRO – Transforming NASA Earth Observations into Smarter Agricultural Decisions

Climate change is increasingly challenging agricultural production worldwide. Rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall patterns, prolonged droughts, excessive precipitation, and soil degradation make agricultural planning more complex and uncertain. Farmers, especially small family producers, often lack accessible tools to understand environmental changes and make informed decisions about when and what to plant.

ClimateAgro is a digital agricultural decision-support platform designed to transform real environmental data and NASA Earth observation information into accessible, practical insights for farmers.

Developed using Manus AI, ClimateAgro already has a navigable application prototype that integrates real environmental data and allows users to explore climate conditions according to their selected city or agricultural property.

The platform aims to help farmers understand local climate patterns through historical temperature variations, rainfall behavior, dry and wet periods, and conditions that may affect agricultural productivity. By analyzing these environmental patterns, ClimateAgro seeks to identify suitable planting periods, potential agricultural vulnerabilities, and opportunities to adapt cultivation practices to changing climate and water conditions.

An important future development of the project is an intelligent alert system designed to notify farmers about potentially unfavorable conditions, including prolonged drought, excessive rainfall, extreme temperatures, and periods of increased crop vulnerability. The platform also intends to indicate when alternative agricultural strategies should be evaluated, supporting more resilient planting decisions and crop rotation planning.

ClimateAgro's long-term vision is to incorporate comparative agricultural analyses and recommendations for crop rotation strategies. These recommendations will consider regional environmental conditions, water availability, climate history, and soil conservation principles, helping farmers explore alternatives that may improve soil health, reduce water pressure, and increase agricultural resilience.

The project recognizes that each agricultural region has unique environmental, economic, and social characteristics. Therefore, ClimateAgro is conceived as a decision-support tool rather than an automatic prescription system. Its purpose is to provide scientific evidence and useful information while preserving the essential role of farmers, agricultural technicians, and local specialists in making final decisions.

By connecting NASA Earth observations with local agricultural realities, ClimateAgro seeks to make scientific knowledge more accessible and useful to small family farmers, large agricultural producers, cooperatives, researchers, students, and agricultural professionals.

Our mission is to transform environmental data into better agricultural decisions, helping farmers plant at the right time, under more favorable conditions, while contributing to soil conservation, responsible water use, and global food security.

ClimateAgro represents a step toward a more sustainable, informed, and climate-resilient agricultural future, demonstrating how space-based science can generate meaningful solutions for life on Earth.
dataRefs: The GPM mission and its IMERG product provide global precipitation rate and accumulation estimates. These help assess rainfall reliability, extreme‑storm frequency, erosion risk, water input to soils, and long‑term trends in field moisture. IMERG is valuable for comparing rotation strategies under different precipitation scenarios. (Worldview IMERG layers can be downloaded directly as high‑resolution images.)

Reflectance, NDVI, Vegetation Indices: Landsat (30‑meter resolution) and MODIS/VIIRS (250–1000 m) provide corrected reflectance, NDVI, vegetation indices, and indicators of plant stress, bare ground, and seasonal change. These datasets allow participants to map crop vigor, track seasonal transitions, detect high‑stress periods, and compare rotation options visually.

Agroclimatology & Meteorological Data: NASA POWER provides accessible solar, meteorological, and climatology datasets used widely in agriculture. The datasets include temperature, humidity, radiation, and derived indicators that help estimate crop water use, growing‑season conditions, frost risk, and climate suitability for potential rotation crops.

Soil Data: SSURGO (field‑scale) and STATSGO2 (regional‑scale) provide detailed soil attributes such as texture, organic matter, drainage class, hydrologic soil group, erosion‑risk factors, restrictive layers, and water‑holding capacity. These data complement NASA observations by enabling accurate, location‑specific assessments of soil health, erosion potential, infiltration dynamics, and crop suitability. Integrating SSURGO with NASA datasets can help SI models produce more grounded and agronomically meaningful rotation suggestions.
projectRefs: ERA5 is a global reanalysis dataset that provides hourly climate variables such as temperature, precipitation, wind, humidity, soil temperature, and radiation. Participants may use ERA5 to fill gaps where local weather stations are sparse, analyze long‑term climate trends, build temporal features for SI models, and contextualize NASA Earth observations with continuous climate time series.
